thread:
lina: Observed a new dup case in onboarding sampleapp. Steps: generate -> 429 during token rotation -> sdk refresh -> immediate retry -> webhook consumer sees two deliveries. Both payloads identical but different gen ids.
omar: thanks. can you paste the compact repro and the sdk logs? curious if sdk replayed without jitter.
lina: repro snippet (sanitized):
```
OUT: POST /v1/generate id=req-99 bodyHash=abc
IN: 429 {"error":"rate_limited"}
SDK: start auth.refresh()
SDK: auth.refresh() ok
OUT: POST /v1/generate id=req-99 bodyHash=abc
IN: 200 {"id":"gen_1"}
WEBHOOK: gen_1
WEBHOOK: gen_2 (~120ms later)
```
dave: so server accepted two different generations even though bodyHash matches. consumer dedupe by payload content; here it was identical but gen ids differed so dedupe failed.
lina: right. sampleapp didn't set any idempotency header for generate flows. we relied on server/user heuristics.
omar: options: (A) change sampleapp to emit X-Idempotency-Key for all user-visible generation calls, (B) SDK-level inflight-guard that keeps a short-lived map of request-hashes to "inflight" and drops/merges immediate retries, (C) post-refresh retry jitter/backoff.
dave: I'd rather not force everyone to remember headers. An inflight-guard in SDK would reduce surprises. Idea: keep a 2s LRU set of hashes; if retry happens within that window, skip actual send and just surface cached response if available. Make it opt-out.
omar: inflight-guard helps but adds state and possible memory leaks on high QPS clients. Another approach: small randomized delay after auth refresh before retry, to reduce race. Could combine both.
lina: agreed. Also note streaming callers (resume semantics) can't tolerate the delay. We should disable inflight-guard and jitter for streaming endpoints.
dave: propose concrete defaults so engs can test: authRefreshRetryDelayMs = 120 (with +/- 80ms uniform jitter), inflightGuardWindowMs = 2000, enableInflightGuard = "opt-in" (false by default), inflightGuardMemoryLimit = 10000 entries.
omar: I suggest making inflight-guard opt-in but enable a lightweight post-refresh jitter by default. Jitter should be configurable and safe for non-streaming calls.
lina: also request better telemetry: emit event `sdk.retry.post_auth` with tags: reason=auth_refresh, hashed_body, attempt_count. That'll let us quantify how often dupes originate from refresh flow.
dave: for sampleapp quick fix: add X-Idempotency-Key header based on user-id+request-hash and update consumer to dedupe by that header when present.
ops-bot: created ticket #6124 "devex: auth-refresh dupes - SDK inflight-guard + post-refresh jitter + telemetry"
omar: I'll open an SDK PR for default jitter + telemetry. dave, can you propose a minimal inflight-guard prototype behind a feature flag?
dave: yes, will draft a small change and a local perf test.
lina: I'll update the onboarding doc to explicitly call out generators: "If your request triggers external side-effects (webhooks, emails), include an idempotency header or rely on server-side dedupe." Add sampleapp PR linking #6124 and attach repro script.
omar: one more edge: token refresh implementations that rotate keys across cluster nodes could still cause effective duplicate acceptance if servers don't check idempotency or body hash. So server-side dedupe recommended too.
dave: agreed. We'll coordinate with SRE to run a quick test harness after PRs land. For config names let's use: `authRefreshRetryDelayMs`, `authRefreshRetryJitterMsRange`, `enableInflightGuard` and `inflightGuardWindowMs`.
lina: thanks all. tiny followups: please make jitter disabled for streaming and expose the toggle in SDK opts. I'll file a short follow-up if SRE sees anything odd. :thumbsup:
